intro: Your 12-week program, daily micro-habits, the mission ladder, a 30-day tracker, and the weekly review. Start on one row; never all at once.
How to run the plan: do the 5-minute drill from the current week daily, tick the 30-day tracker with the checkmark character, and answer the weekly review.

weeks.drill: Hold calm eye contact for three seconds and smile at one person.
weeks.mission: Greet five people today and notice how each one responds.
weeks.body: Stand tall and unclench your jaw before every interaction.
weeks.brain: Write one sentence about a moment when someone smiled back.
weeks.culture: Read one page about how first impressions form.

weeks.drill: Ask one stranger a simple question about the place you are in.
weeks.mission: Start three short chats at a cafe, shop, or gym.
weeks.body: Walk 20 minutes outdoors and greet one passerby.
weeks.brain: Keep a list of three easy opening questions that fit almost anywhere.
weeks.culture: Listen to a ten-minute podcast about everyday conversation.

weeks.drill: Paraphrase the last thing someone said before you reply.
weeks.mission: Have one ten-minute talk where you ask two follow-up questions.
weeks.body: Put your phone away and face the speaker during one meal.
weeks.brain: Write down one thing you learned from each real conversation.
weeks.culture: Watch a short interview and note how the interviewer follows up.

weeks.drill: Send one low-pressure invitation text each morning.
weeks.mission: Invite two people to a specific activity this week.
weeks.body: Prepare a clean, simple outfit for the invitation outing.
weeks.brain: Plan three easy outing ideas with a time and a place.
weeks.culture: Read one page on why small favors and invitations build trust.

weeks.drill: Tell one sixty-second story with a beginning, a turn, and an end.
weeks.mission: Share a short story with a friend and ask for one of theirs.
weeks.body: Practise the story aloud once while walking.
weeks.brain: Write the three beats of one story you already love.
weeks.culture: Watch a five-minute art video and retell its story from memory.

weeks.drill: Do ten push-ups or a five-minute stretch after waking.
weeks.mission: Ask one trusted person for honest feedback on your style.
weeks.body: Lift twice, sleep by eleven three nights, and tidy your hair or grooming.
weeks.brain: Track sleep hours and morning energy on each day of the week.
weeks.culture: Read one short article on fit, grooming, and simple style.

weeks.drill: Practise one clear ask out loud: what, when, and why.
weeks.mission: Make one real request you have been avoiding.
weeks.body: Breathe out slowly for five minutes before the ask.
weeks.brain: Write your best alternative and your walk-away point.
weeks.culture: Listen to a fifteen-minute negotiation podcast clip.

weeks.drill: Explain one idea aloud for two minutes without notes.
weeks.mission: Present or teach something to a small group.
weeks.body: Practise posture and pace in front of a mirror once.
weeks.brain: Make three slides or one handout with one idea each.
weeks.culture: Watch a five-minute explainer and copy its structure.

weeks.drill: Send one friendly check-in message each day.
weeks.mission: Organize a small hangout with three to five people.
weeks.body: Clean and set up one room, and prepare simple food and water.
weeks.brain: Write a short plan: arrival, activity, food, and end time.
weeks.culture: Learn one dinner-party fact you can share naturally.

weeks.drill: Read ten minutes or watch one short art video.
weeks.mission: Visit a museum or gallery and talk about one work.
weeks.body: Walk through the museum slowly for forty-five minutes.
weeks.brain: Write three sentences about one artwork from memory.
weeks.culture: Finish one short book or one long chapter.

weeks.drill: Write one boundary sentence: I need this, or I will not accept that.
weeks.mission: Have one honest conversation you have been postponing.
weeks.body: Sleep well and eat before the talk, and avoid alcohol.
weeks.brain: Write the other person's view in two fair sentences.
weeks.culture: Read one short piece on repair after conflict.

weeks.drill: Review your tracker and tick one win each morning.
weeks.mission: Thank two people who helped you this quarter.
weeks.body: Book a checkup or a workout plan for the next month.
weeks.brain: Write a one-page review: wins, lessons, and three next goals.
weeks.culture: Pick your next book and your next museum visit.

microHabits.habit: Stand tall and reset your shoulders once an hour.
Take five slow breaths with long exhales before a hard task.
Write two lines about the day's strongest feeling.
Do one set of push-ups or squats after waking.
Set a 10:30 pm alarm and turn lights out by 11.
Read two pages of a real book before bed.
Send one short thank-you text to a different person.
Ask one person a genuine question and listen to the answer.
Walk for two minutes outdoors after lunch.
Eat one meal a day with your phone in another room.

missionLadder.mission: Make eye contact and smile at one person.
missionLadder.why: Exposure: a tiny safe rep teaches the brain that social contact is not a threat.

missionLadder.mission: Say a quick hello to one stranger.
missionLadder.why: Mere exposure: repeated neutral contact makes the same action feel more familiar and less risky.

missionLadder.mission: Ask a stranger one simple question.
missionLadder.why: Behavioral rehearsal: practising the skill at low stakes builds a script you can reuse.

missionLadder.mission: Have a two-minute chat with a stranger.
missionLadder.why: Successive approximation: each small step makes the next, slightly harder step easier to start.
Mastery experiences: completing a real invitation builds self-efficacy, the belief that you can do it again.

missionLadder.mission: Share one honest story with a friend.
missionLadder.why: Self-disclosure and reciprocity: gradual openness invites openness back and deepens trust.

missionLadder.mission: Make a clear ask or negotiate one small thing.
missionLadder.why: Exposure with feedback: surviving the ask weakens avoidance and shows that rejection is survivable.

missionLadder.mission: Give a short talk or teach a small group.
missionLadder.why: Mastery plus audience feedback: visible reps turn shaky knowledge into confident performance.
Role rehearsal: planning and hosting practise the identity and logistics of a socially active person.
Cumulative mastery: stacked wins make a high-pressure social role feel normal and repeatable.

review.q: What worked this week, and why?
What felt fake or forced, and what will you change?
Who did you connect with, and how did it feel?
What do your body data say about sleep, energy, and training?
What is the one change you will make next week?
